result.title: Reward Inflation: A Healthy Stimulus for Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Reward serves as the primary learning signal in reinforcement learning (RL). However, while reward magnitudes are typically held fixed throughout training, their temporal modulation remains underexplored. In this paper, we propose reward inflation, a gradual scaling of rewards over the course of training, and show that it can act as a healthy stimulus for RL. Theoretically, reward inflation induces an implicit recency weighting that upweights recent transitions during policy updates, enabling faster adaptation. We further show that, by sustaining gradient signals as the policy saturates, reward inflation suppresses the emergence of dormant neurons and helps preserve plasticity. Empirical results on ALE games and MuJoCo tasks corroborate these findings, showing that an appropriate level of reward inflation benefits a broad range of tasks. Finally, we introduce Fed, an adaptive variant that adjusts the inflation level on the fly, and find that it often improves upon fixed inflation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「reward inflation」：在 RL 训练过程中逐步放大奖励幅度，从理论上说明它等价于对近期 transition 的隐式重加权，并将之与维持梯度信号、抑制 dormant neuron、保持可塑性联系起来；在 ALE 与 MuJoCo 上验证适当膨胀有益，并提出自适应调节膨胀程度的 Fed 变体。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽不涉及视觉推理，但其「训练过程中随策略饱和动态调节奖励尺度以维持梯度与可塑性」的机制，可能与 VLM 推理中长轨迹训练的信号衰减、贡献分配和动态计算调节有可供核查的迁移线索。
